note: OPI-style practice prompts drafted by an LLM (not official OPI or DLPT items). Self-rating checklists are paraphrased from the public-domain ILR Skill Level Descriptions for Speaking.
checklistSource: Interagency Language Roundtable Skill Level Descriptions — Speaking (U.S. Government, public domain), https://www.govtilr.org/Skills/ILRscale2.htm

checklist: I can say memorized words and set phrases for basic needs, like greetings, numbers and polite words.
I can name common everyday objects, colors, days and family members.
I mostly speak in single words or short memorized phrases, not in sentences of my own.
People who are used to learners often have trouble understanding me.
questions: Accept a one-word answer; model a full sentence back.
Country name alone is fine at this level.
What is this? (point to an object)
How many people are in your family?
朝ごはんに何を食べましたか。
What did you eat for breakfast?
（お店で）いらっしゃいませ。何にしますか。
(At a shop) Welcome. What would you like?
Learner orders one item: 〜をください.
日本語は楽しいですか。
ありがとうございました。

checklist: I can handle simple face-to-face situations like ordering food, buying things, asking directions and getting a room.
I can ask and answer simple questions about familiar topics such as myself, my family and my daily routine.
I can make my own short sentences, though I make frequent mistakes in grammar and pronunciation.
A native speaker used to foreigners can understand me, with some effort and repetition.
questions: 自己紹介をしてください。
今日はどうやってここに来ましたか。
How did you get here today?
Transport vocabulary: 電車で, 車で.
毎日、何時に起きますか。それから何をしますか。
What time do you get up every day? What do you do next?
週末はたいてい何をしますか。
What do you usually do on weekends?
あなたの町について教えてください。
先週の週末、何をしましたか。
What did you do last weekend?
Push for past narration in connected sentences (level 1+/2).
どうして日本語を勉強していますか。
Reasons with から; probes beyond memorized material.
（駅で）すみません、どうしましたか。
(At a station) Excuse me, can I help?
Learner asks how to get to a place and confirms.
（レストランで）ご注文はお決まりですか。
(At a restaurant) Are you ready to order?
Order two things and ask a simple question.
今日はこのあと何をしますか。
What will you do after this?

checklist: I can take care of most everyday and travel needs, including small complications like a lost item or a wrong order.
I can talk about my background, work and interests in some detail, and can narrate simple past events.
I sometimes manage to link sentences, but I often break down when I try to explain or describe at length.
My vocabulary for concrete topics is growing, but I still fall back on simple structures.
questions: 最近、何か楽しいことがありましたか。
あなたの仕事（勉強）について詳しく教えてください。
Tell me about your work (studies) in detail.
Sustained description of a familiar topic.
初めて日本に来たときのことを話してください。
Tell me about when you first came to Japan.
あなたの国と日本の違いは何だと思いますか。
What differences do you see between your country and Japan?
もし一か月休みがあったら、何をしたいですか。
If you had a month off, what would you want to do?
その理由を詳しく説明してください。
Please explain your reason in detail.
（ホテルで）お部屋に何か問題がございましたか。
(At a hotel) Was there a problem with your room?
Complication: the air conditioner is broken; ask for a solution.
日本でおすすめの場所はありますか。
Any place in Japan you'd recommend?
今日はありがとうございました。

checklist: I can handle routine social and work demands, including giving instructions and describing situations.
I can narrate and describe in the past, present and future with paragraphs of connected speech.
I can talk about current events, my job and my interests with reasonable accuracy, though I lack precision on complex topics.
Native speakers not used to foreigners can usually understand me, even when my grammar is imperfect.
questions: お仕事は今、忙しいですか。
Is work busy at the moment?
あなたの一日の仕事の流れを説明してください。
Explain the flow of a typical workday.
最近見たニュースで印象に残ったものを教えてください。
Tell me about a recent news story that stuck with you.
今までで一番大変だった経験について話してください。
Talk about the hardest experience you've had.
五年後、どんな生活をしていると思いますか。
What do you think your life will be like in five years?
在宅勤務のメリットとデメリットは何だと思いますか。
What are the pros and cons of working from home?
その問題を解決するには、どうすればいいと思いますか。
How do you think that problem could be solved?
（職場で）来週の会議の場所が変わったので、チームに説明してください。
(At work) The meeting venue changed; explain to your team.
Give instructions clearly and handle a question.
（店で）買った商品が壊れていました。店員と交渉してください。
(At a shop) The item you bought is broken. Negotiate with the clerk.
日本語の勉強で工夫していることはありますか。
Any tricks you use for studying Japanese?
お時間をいただき、ありがとうございました。

checklist: I can meet most work demands and often speak effectively on abstract topics, though not consistently.
I can support an opinion and state a hypothesis some of the time, but my accuracy drops under pressure.
I understand and use a fairly wide range of vocabulary and can often find a way around a missing word.
Errors in grammar or word choice sometimes appear in complex structures but rarely block understanding.
questions: 最近、何か新しく始めたことはありますか。
Have you started anything new lately?
あなたの専門分野について、専門外の人にわかるように説明してください。
Explain your field so that a non-specialist can understand.
日本の少子化について、どう考えますか。
What do you think about Japan's declining birth rate?
反対の立場の人を説得するとしたら、どう話しますか。
If you had to persuade someone with the opposite view, what would you say?
もしその政策が失敗したら、どんな影響があると思いますか。
If that policy failed, what effects would you expect?
技術の進歩は人間関係をどう変えたと思いますか。
How do you think technology has changed human relationships?
（会議で）予算削減の案に反対の意見を丁寧に述べてください。
(Meeting) Politely state your opposition to a budget-cut plan.
（取引先に）納期が遅れることを説明し、謝罪してください。
(To a client) Explain and apologize for a delivery delay.
休みの日はどう過ごすのが好きですか。
How do you like to spend days off?
Relax back to a familiar topic.
本日はありがとうございました。

checklist: I can take part effectively in most formal and informal conversations on practical, social and professional topics.
I can support opinions, argue a position and hypothesize on abstract topics with structured, extended discourse.
My errors almost never interfere with understanding or disturb a native speaker.
I can adjust my register, including keigo, to fit the situation.
questions: 今日はお忙しい中、ありがとうございます。最近いかがですか。
Thank you for making time today. How have you been?
グローバル化が日本の地方に与える影響について、ご意見をお聞かせください。
Please share your views on how globalization affects regional Japan.
AIの発展によって、教育はどう変わるべきだと思いますか。
How should education change as AI develops?
日米同盟の今後の課題は何だとお考えですか。
What do you see as future challenges for the Japan–U.S. alliance?
その主張に対する最も強い反論は何でしょうか。それにどう答えますか。
What is the strongest counterargument, and how would you answer it?
仮に法律でそれを禁止した場合、どのような問題が起こり得ますか。
If it were banned by law, what problems might arise?
（公式の場で）日本側の担当者に、計画の変更を説明し、理解を求めてください。
(Formal setting) Explain a plan change to your Japanese counterpart and seek their understanding.
（記者会見で）事故について事実を説明し、質問に答えてください。
(Press conference) State the facts about an incident and answer questions.
日本語を使っていて、一番やりがいを感じるのはどんなときですか。
When do you find using Japanese most rewarding?
本日は貴重なお時間をいただき、誠にありがとうございました。
Thank you sincerely for your valuable time today.
